highlights.headline: Flash Eurobarometer: Europeans call for stronger action on children's online safety, democratic resilience, defence, and the energy transition
highlights.summary: European Commission Press release Brussels, 13 Jul 2026 A new Eurobarometer survey released today shows that Europeans are overwhelmingly concerned about all the risks children face on social media. Against the backdrop of increasing reliance on social media, citizens see the need for better protection and tougher action to tackle disinformation.

items.title: World Cup: Balogun red and expansion keep FIFA in spotlight
items.description: The fallout from Folarin Balogun's red card reversal continues as reports suggest the chairman of FIFA’s disciplinary committee made the decision unilaterally. Meanwhile, the World Cup could be set to expand once more.

items.title: Wildfire raging south of Paris could have been set deliberately, says minister
items.description: The interior minister has said the fire near Paris could have been set deliberately and two people have been arrested.

items.title: Briton tells of surviving Spain wildfire in car as wife and friends died trying to run to safety
items.description: Malcolm Timbrell's wife and their friends are thought to have died when a devastating wildfire tore through their village in Spain.

items.title: Ukraine, 9 countries form ballistic missile defense coalition
items.description: Ukraine and nine European countries launched a coalition to protect Europe from ballistic missiles, drawing on Kyiv’s wartime experience.

sections.title: Beyond Climate & EU — World News Highlights

items.title: EU experts urge social media restrictions for kids under 13
items.description: An expert panel has recommended limiting access to social media for young children across the EU. The European Commission is expected to present a proposal for legislation on the issue in the coming months.

items.title: Hungary parliament votes to remove president from office
items.description: Tamás Sulyok was widely seen as a loyalist of former prime minister Viktor Orbán, who lost power in April after 16 years.

items.title: Hungary: Lawmakers pass law to oust Orban ally president
items.description: The Hungarian parliament continued its attempts to leave the Viktor Orban era behind the country by moving to oust President Tamas Sulyok.

items.title: Gaza Strip: EU conference pledges €900m in donations
items.description: The conference in Brussels was attended by Palestinian representatives. The EU's top diplomat said the bloc's support depends on reforms in the Palestinian Authority.

items.title: EU approves new passenger rights for air travel
items.description: EU ministers have approved a set of reforms giving more rights to air travelers. Among other things, compensation claims are to be made easier.
